title: Bumdra Trek
subtitle: A short cliff-camp trek above Paro, ending at the Tiger's Nest
overview: The Bumdra Trek is the ideal short trek for travellers who want a genuine camping night in the mountains without committing to a long expedition. From the Sang Choekhor Buddhist College the trail climbs through village settlements and forests of varied species to Bumdra Monastery — the Cave of a Thousand Prayers — where you camp for the night high above the Paro valley.

The following morning you descend through the forest to Taktshang, the Tiger's Nest Monastery, one of the most sacred sites in the Buddhist world. It is a rare route that packs ridge-top camping, monasteries and Bhutan's most iconic landmark into a short four-day trip, arrival and departure days included.
highlights: Camp at Bumdra Monastery, the Cave of a Thousand Prayers
Climb to 4,000 m for a spectacular view of the Himalayan range
Descend to the Tiger's Nest (Taktshang) from above
Forests of blue pine and rhododendron the whole way

days.title: Arrival at Paro
days.description: On your flight to Paro the journey affords spectacular views of the snow-capped Himalaya, including Jomolhari and Jichu Drake. Our representative will receive you at Paro Airport. If you arrive before noon you can start your trip after lunch, visiting the 8th-century Kyichu Lhakhang, one of the oldest Buddhist temples in the kingdom. In the evening, explore the town. Overnight in Paro.

days.title: Sang Choekhor — Bumdra
days.description: Drive to Sang Choekhor Buddhist College at 2,700 m, where our trek starts. Passing through village settlements and entering forests of varied species, the trail leads us to Choe Choe Tse Lhakhang. After three to four hours of normal trekking we reach Bumdra Monastery, the Cave of a Thousand Prayers; our camp for the night is here. We usually arrive by lunch, and afterwards visit the monastery and climb the mountain at 4,000 m before returning to camp. From the summit, the view of the Himalayan range is spectacular.

days.title: Bumdra — Taktshang — Paro
days.description: After breakfast we descend gradually to the valley on a winding trail through forests of pine and rhododendron. After one to two hours we catch a glimpse of the roof of a temple — the legendary Taktshang, the Tiger's Nest Monastery. An hour later we find ourselves at its entrance. Guru Rinpoche, the 8th-century Buddhist saint, is said to have flown here on the back of a tigress to meditate. From the temple the view of the Paro valley is splendid. Descend to Paro and walk freely in the town in the evening. Overnight in a hotel in Paro.

days.title: Departure
days.description: After breakfast, we see you off at the airport.

title: Druk Path Trek
subtitle: Bhutan's classic lake-and-ridge trek between Paro and Thimphu
overview: The Druk Path is Bhutan's best-loved trek — short enough for a first expedition, high enough to feel truly remote. Over five trekking days the trail crosses the mountains between the Paro and Thimphu valleys, following ridgelines past a string of lakes known for their giant trout.

Bracketed by cultural days in the Paro and Thimphu valleys — including the hike to the Tiger's Nest — it is the ideal introduction to camping treks in the Himalaya, with thick alpine forest, dwarf rhododendron, yak-herder camps and, weather permitting, views of Bhutan's highest peaks.
highlights: Camp beside Jimilangtso Lake, famed for its giant trout
Trout fishing country at Simkota Lake, or push on to Labana
Views of Gangkar Puensum, the world's highest unclimbed peak
Hike to the Tiger's Nest on the acclimatisation day

days.title: Arrival at Paro
days.description: On your flight to Paro the journey affords spectacular views of the snow-capped Himalaya, including Jomolhari and Jichu Drake. If you fly via Delhi or Kathmandu you may also see Everest and Kanchenjunga. Our representative will receive you at Paro Airport. If you arrive before noon you can start your trip after lunch, visiting the 8th-century Kyichu Lhakhang, one of the oldest Buddhist temples in the kingdom. In the evening, explore the town and plunge into Bhutan's urban life. Overnight in Paro.

days.title: Hike to Taktshang Monastery
days.description: The morning hike to Taktshang, the Tiger's Nest, is a refreshing and exciting one. Perched on a rocky ledge 3,000 ft above the valley floor, the monastery was founded by Guru Padmasambhava, who is believed to have come here on the back of a tigress from Khengpajong in the Kurtoe region to meditate, and later converted the Paro valley to Buddhism. Lunch at the Taktshang cafeteria, then a free stroll in the town and nearby villages. Overnight in Paro.

days.title: Paro — Jele Dzong (trek starts)
days.description: Start from the hotel around 8–9 am for the trek start point. This is a short trekking day of approximately 7 km, to an elevation of 2,576 m. The trail is rather gradual all the way to camp. The scenic Paro valley, with snow-capped mountains standing behind the valley floor, is the characteristic feature of the day.

days.title: Jele Dzong — Jangchulakha
days.description: Stretching for about 10 km to an elevation of 3,879 m, the day begins with about an hour and a half of climbing and then ascends gentle slopes. The trek passes through thick alpine forest and dwarf rhododendron. You may see yaks and yak herders along the way and around your campsite.

days.title: Jangchulakha — Jimilangtso
days.description: Covering 11 km at a height of 4,040 m, the trail follows the ridge. On a clear day the views of the mountains and valleys are beautiful. The campsite is close to Jimilangtso Lake, known for the existence of giant trout. Overnight at 3,800 m.

days.title: Jimilangtso — Simkota / Labana
days.description: At an altitude of 4,150 m, the day extends to 11–13 km. The trail takes you through dwarf rhododendron and past Janetso Lake. You may come across yak-herder campgrounds and get a glimpse of a nomad's life. The campsite is close to Simkota Lake, popular for trout fishing — or continue another hour to Labana, the highest campsite of the entire trek.

days.title: Simkota / Labana — Phajoding — Thimphu
days.description: Requiring a gradual climb through the ridges, the trek is about 10 km. Under a clear sky you will have a spectacular view of Mount Gangkar Puensum, the highest mountain in Bhutan and the highest unclimbed peak in the world, and a sight of the wider Himalayan ranges. From here the trail takes you downhill via Phajoding to Thimphu for the night.

days.title: Thimphu — Paro
days.description: After breakfast visit the National Memorial Chorten, one of the main iconic spots in Thimphu. Proceed to Kuensel Phodrang and visit the folk heritage museum, then walk along the craft market. After lunch visit the Centenary Farmers' Market and stop at the CSI market on the way to Paro. Overnight in Paro.

days.title: Departure
days.description: After breakfast, we see you off at the airport.

title: Dagala Thousand Lakes Trek
subtitle: High meadows and a scatter of alpine lakes south of Thimphu
overview: The Dagala Thousand Lakes Trek comprises mostly short trekking days interspersed with a few long, steep climbs. Beginning in Genekha near Thimphu and concluding in Chamgang, the trail winds through pristine forest and leads to numerous stunning high-altitude lakes.

As you hike past crystal-clear waters and untouched landscapes you are rewarded with breathtaking panoramic views of the Himalaya. On a clear day you can spot Mount Everest, Jomolhari, Kanchenjunga, Masagang, Jichu Drake and more. Along the way you also pass Bhutanese villages, offering a glimpse into the country's traditional way of life.
highlights: A landscape dotted with clear high-altitude lakes
Panorama of Everest, Kanchenjunga, Jomolhari and Jichu Drake
Blooming wildflowers and wild asparagus in spring
A full rest day to explore the lakes around Labatama

days.title: Arrival at Paro
days.description: On your flight to Paro the journey affords spectacular views of the snow-capped Himalaya, including the Jomolhari and Jichu Drake peaks. Our representative will receive you at Paro Airport. If you arrive before noon you can start your trip after lunch, visiting the 8th-century Kyichu Lhakhang, one of the oldest Buddhist temples in the kingdom, built by the Tibetan king Songtsen Gampo. In the evening you can explore the town. Overnight in Paro.

days.title: Hike to Taktshang Monastery
days.description: The morning hike to Taktshang, the Tiger's Nest, is a refreshing and exciting one. Perched on a rocky ledge 3,000 ft above the valley floor, the monastery was founded by the great Buddhist saint Guru Padmasambhava. The hike to the viewpoint makes a fine half-day excursion with beautiful views of the Paro valley. Rest at the Taktshang cafeteria for lunch, then take a free stroll in town and the nearby village settlements. Overnight in Paro.

days.title: Drive to Genekha, trek to Kepchen
days.description: We drive one to one-and-a-half hours to the start of the trek. Today's trail winds through terraced fields and conifer forest. From Genekha village (2,800 m) a short descent leads to the river, then you climb to a vast rock platform at 3,350 m with a breathtaking panoramic view of the valley below. After another two hours you arrive at Kepchen, nestled amid yak pastures at about 3,390 m. Overnight at camp.

days.title: Kepchen — Labatama
days.description: Today's trek takes you through blooming wildflowers, wild asparagus in spring, and vast meadows. Weaving past tiny streams, the trail ascends gently through scattered birch and rhododendron to Pagalabtsa Pass (4,250 m), marked by towering cairns, with spectacular views of Kanchenjunga in Sikkim and several Bhutanese Himalayan peaks. As you descend, the panorama of the entire Dagala range unfolds, dotted with meadows and yak-herder camps. Overnight at camp.

days.title: Labatama halt and rest day
days.description: Spend a leisurely day relaxing and exploring the picturesque Labatama valley. For those feeling adventurous, a range of day excursions is available to Relitsho, Hentsho or Jametsho Lake. Overnight at camp.

days.title: Labatama — Pankha
days.description: Today's trail ascends along the western side of Dala Tsho lake to a saddle at 4,520 m, where you can soak in breathtaking views of Everest, Kanchenjunga, Jomolhari, Jichu Drake, Tshering Gang, Khangbum, Masang Gang, Tshenda Gang and Gangche Ta. For an even more spectacular vantage point you can climb a nearby peak at 4,720 m. From the saddle the trail descends past yak-herder huts to Docha Chhu, then follows the river to your campsite at Pankha. Overnight at camp.

days.title: Pankha — Chamgang (trek ends)
days.description: The last day of the trek, but the climbing is not over: you ascend gradually to a mountain pass at 4,300 m — steady rather than steep. From there the trail undulates with several ups and downs before descending steeply to Chamgang (2,640 m), where the vehicle picks you up for the drive to Thimphu. In the evening you are free to stroll around the town. Overnight at the hotel.

days.title: Departure
days.description: After breakfast, drive to the airport for a final goodbye.

title: Jomolhari Round Trek
subtitle: The Dodhina route — the full Jomolhari circuit over two high passes
overview: Also known as the Dodhina Trek, this is the classic Jomolhari circuit. From Shana the trail climbs along the Pa Chhu to Jangothang at the foot of Mt. Jomolhari, then loops over the Nyile La (4,700 m) and Yeli La (4,820 m) with grandstand views of Jomolhari, Jichu Drake, Tshering Gang, Gangchen Ta and Masang Gang.

Past the fortress of Lingshi Dzong the route descends the Mo Chhu and Thimphu river valleys through rhododendron, juniper and alpine vegetation, with cascading waterfalls, to finish at Barshong and a short drive out to the road.
highlights: Base camp beneath Mt. Jomolhari at Jangothang (4,040 m)
Cross the Nyile La (4,700 m) and Yeli La (4,820 m)
Panoramic views of Lingshi Dzong and its valley
Cascading waterfalls on the descent to Barshong

days.title: Arrival at Paro
days.description: On your flight to Paro the journey affords spectacular views of the snow-capped Himalaya, including Jomolhari and Jichu Drake. Our representative will receive you at the airport. If you arrive before noon you can start your trip after lunch, visiting the 8th-century Kyichu Lhakhang, one of the oldest Buddhist temples in the kingdom. In the evening, explore the town. Overnight in Paro.

days.title: Hike to Taktshang Monastery
days.description: The morning hike to the Tiger's Nest, perched on a rocky ledge 3,000 ft above the valley floor, makes a fine half-day excursion with beautiful views of the Paro valley. Descend from the monastery and rest at the Taktshang cafeteria for lunch, then take a free stroll in the town and the nearby village settlements. Overnight in Paro.

days.title: Shana — Soi Thangthangkha
days.description: After an early breakfast we drive two to three hours to Shana, the trek start point. The trek follows the Pa Chhu, climbing and descending through pine, oak and spruce forest. After crossing the bridge the team stops for a hot lunch. Afterwards we climb along the bank of the river through rhododendron forest, cross the river again, and reach the campsite at 3,750 m.

days.title: Soi Thangthangkha — Jangothang
days.description: The trail involves gentle climbs before you reach the army camp. Following the river above the tree line, the trek presents stunning views of the surrounding peaks. For lunch we stop at a yak herder's camp. A short walk into the valley brings you to Jangothang at 4,040 m, where we pitch base camp. The views of Mt. Jomolhari and Jichu Drake are splendid.

days.title: Jangothang (base camp) halt
days.description: To acclimatise for the following day's highest climb on this trek, we rest and explore the nearby areas. Mountains and lakes offer exciting sites to explore.

days.title: Jangothang — Lingshi
days.description: Following the stream for half an hour, we cross the bridge to the right and start the climb to the first ridge, from where you have a breathtaking view of Jomolhari, Jichu Drake and Tshering Gang. Continue into the valley, almost flat for a while, until the climb to the Nyile La begins at 4,700 m. Conquering the pass, the trail descends gradually to Lingshi camp, relishing the panoramic view of the peaks and Lingshi Dzong. Camp at 4,000 m.

days.title: Lingshi — Shodu
days.description: The Laya–Gasa route leaves the Jomolhari trek here. The trail climbs to a small chorten on a ridge above camp, turns south and continues up the deep Mo Chhu valley. It passes through the treeless valley, climbing steadily a short distance above the Mo Chhu, then crosses the river and climbs steeply for two hours to the Yeli La at 4,820 m. From the pass, on a clear day, you can see Jomolhari, Gangchen Ta, Tshering Gang and Masang Gang. Descend alongside a stream to a shelter and then further downstream to camp at Shodu (4,100 m), alongside a meadow with a chorten.

days.title: Shodu — Barshong (trek ends)
days.description: The route enters back below the tree line. Following the Wang Chhu, the Thimphu river, the trail descends through forests of rhododendron, juniper and alpine vegetation. Passing along a ridge, cascades of waterfall present a breathtaking view. A hot lunch is served by the river bank. After lunch the route takes you to the ruins of Barshong Dzong, reaching camp at 3,600 m — and the end of the trek.

days.title: Barshong — Dodhina — Paro
days.description: After breakfast, drive on a dirt road for two hours until you meet your car on a better road, then drive to Paro for the night.

days.title: Departure
days.description: Drop at the airport, where our team sees you off.

title: Soi Yaksa Trek
subtitle: A wild Jomolhari-region loop over the Bonte La
overview: The Soi Yaksa Trek follows the Pa Chhu deep into the Jomolhari region, passing the junction where an old trading path leads over the Tremo La to Tibet, before pitching base camp at Jangothang beneath Mt. Jomolhari and Jichu Drake.

From there it crosses the Bonte La, the highest pass of the trek, into a valley ringed by impressive rock cliffs, waterfalls, deep side valleys and snow-capped peaks — a genuine high-mountain trek that stays well off the busier trails.
highlights: Camp at the Jomolhari base camp (Jangothang, 4,040 m)
Cross the Bonte La, the trek's 4,890 m high point
The rock cliffs and waterfalls of the Soi Yaksa valley
Views of Mt. Jomolhari and Jichu Drake from the passes

days.title: Arrival at Paro
days.description: On your flight to Paro the journey affords spectacular views of the snow-capped Himalaya, including Jomolhari and Jichu Drake. Our representative will receive you at Paro Airport. If you arrive before noon you can start your trip after lunch, visiting the 8th-century Kyichu Lhakhang, one of the oldest Buddhist temples in the kingdom. In the evening, explore the town. Overnight in Paro.

days.title: Hike to Taktshang Monastery
days.description: The morning hike to the Tiger's Nest is a refreshing and exciting one. Perched on a rocky ledge 3,000 ft above the valley floor, the monastery was founded by Guru Padmasambhava. The hike to the viewpoint makes a fine half-day excursion with beautiful views of the Paro valley. Lunch at the Taktshang cafeteria, then a free stroll in town and the nearby villages. Overnight in Paro.

days.title: Shana — Thangthangkha
days.description: After breakfast we drive about two hours to the trek start point. The trail follows the river through a heavily forested area with a few isolated farmhouses. As we go up, the valley becomes narrower, wilder and steeper, and the trail winds up and down along the drainage. We pass a junction where another path leads over the Tremo La to Tibet — formerly a Bhutanese trading route. We cross several traditional wooden bridges, finally arriving at Thangthangkha. Camp here for the night.

days.title: Thangthangkha — Jangothang (base camp)
days.description: Following the river above the tree line, the trek presents stunning views of the surrounding peaks. For lunch we stop at a yak herder's camp. A short walk into the valley brings you to Jangothang at 4,040 m, where we pitch base camp. The views of Mt. Jomolhari and Jichu Drake are splendid.

days.title: Jangothang halt
days.description: After an arduous trek crossing 1,800 m in three days, we halt a day at Jangothang. To adapt to the height we go for short day hikes to nearby places. Yaks and yak herders will be in your sight frequently. Feel the lush green surrounding environment.

days.title: Jangothang — Soi Yaksa via Bonte La
days.description: We start early today for the highest pass to conquer on our entire trek. The weather in the mountains is settled early in the morning, affording splendid views of the surrounding peaks and beyond. We cross the Bonte La at 4,890 m, the highest point of the trek, marked with several cairns and prayer flags — you may put up some prayer flags of your own here. The campsite in the Soi Yaksa valley is amazing, surrounded by impressive rock cliffs, waterfalls, deep side valleys and snow-capped peaks.

days.title: Soi Yaksa — Thombu Thang
days.description: After passing a village we start an hour of steady climb. The pass, with several cairns and prayer flags, affords a spectacular view of Mt. Jomolhari and Jichu Drake. A gradual descent takes us to Thombu for tonight's camp — the second-highest camp on our trek.

days.title: Thombu Thang — Shana — Paro
days.description: Crossing the valley through a swampy area, we enter a clear trail through rhododendron forest leading up to Thombu La at 4,270 m. The walk along the ridge is one of the best stretches of the trek, passing above the valley floor and affording spectacular views. The trail ends near the military helipad next to the Bhutanese army camp. The last night is in Paro town.

days.title: Departure
days.description: After breakfast, we see you off at the airport.

title: Laya – Lingzhi Trek
subtitle: Deep into the far north to the village of the Layap people
overview: The Laya–Lingzhi Trek is one of Bhutan's great long treks, crossing a series of high passes from the Jomolhari base camp through Lingshi and Chebisa to the isolated village of Laya near the Tibetan border. Along the way you may see herds of takin — Bhutan's national animal — gathered in the Tsharijathang valley.

Laya's people maintain a distinct culture, the women wearing conical bamboo hats decorated with turquoise and silver ornaments. After a full day exploring the village, the trek finishes with a stop at the famous Gasa hot springs, long prized by the Bhutanese for their healing waters.
highlights: Reach the remote village of Laya (3,850 m)
Cross the Shinge La at 4,900 m, the trek's high point
See herds of takin, Bhutan's national animal, at Tsharijathang
Soak in the Gasa hot springs after ten days on the trail

days.title: Arrival at Paro
days.description: On your flight to Paro the journey affords spectacular views of the snow-capped Himalaya, including Jomolhari and Jichu Drake. Our representative will receive you at Paro Airport. If you arrive before noon you can start your trip after lunch, visiting the 8th-century Kyichu Lhakhang. In the evening, explore the town. Overnight in Paro.

days.title: Hike to Taktshang Monastery
days.description: The morning hike to the Tiger's Nest makes a fine half-day excursion with beautiful views of the Paro valley. Lunch at the Taktshang cafeteria, then a free stroll in town and the nearby village settlements. Overnight in Paro.

days.title: Shana — Soe Thangthangkha
days.description: In the morning we drive to Gunitsawa, where there is an army camp, and start our trek. The trail continues uphill through the river valley, which gradually becomes narrower and closes in after some distance. The winding trail with frequent climbs and descents leads us to our campsite in a meadow with a stone shelter at 3,720 m.

days.title: Thangthangkha — Jangothang
days.description: Continue the trail along the Pa Chhu; the valley opens again after crossing a small army outpost. Trekking through the open valley affords views of high ridges and snow-capped mountains, with yaks and yak-herder camps on the valley floor. The day brings us near the ruined fortress at the base of Mt. Jomolhari at 4,040 m. Camp here for the night.

days.title: Jangothang halt
days.description: After two long trekking days you have a good chance to relax under the sun right in front of Jomolhari. If you are interested, you may go further from the base camp and climb to Tsho Phu at 4,300 m. Night at camp.

days.title: Jangothang — Lingshi
days.description: Climb gradually toward the pass through wide pastureland. On your way, depending on the season, you will find yak herders in their camps. Descending from the pass to Lingshi you have a beautiful view of Lingshi Dzong, the valley, Tserim Kang and its glaciers. At 4,150 m, camp in a stone shelter with a built-in fire pit, or in the tent.

days.title: Lingshi — Chebisa
days.description: Today is the shortest of all days on our trip. Upon reaching Chebisa at 3,850 m, having trekked three to four hours, we camp alongside the village settlement. You can visit the village houses and experience Bhutanese rural life.

days.title: Chebisa — Shomuthang
days.description: Trekking through wide pastureland leads up to the Gobu La. Along the way you find some yak herders. Conquering the Gobu La at 4,305 m, we descend to the valley. The campsite is above a river bank, a tributary of the Mo Chhu, at 4,260 m.

days.title: Shomuthang — Robluthang
days.description: We start early, for the trek is a little strenuous. Upon crossing the Jhari La at 4,600 m we descend to the Tsharijathang valley, where you can see herds of takin, the national animal of Bhutan. Camp at Tsharijathang at 4,390 m.

days.title: Robluthang — Lingmithang
days.description: Crossing the Shinge La at 4,900 m, you take a downhill trek following the valley. Lingmithang, a beautiful village under Laya county, offers an opportunity to see people dressed in typical Laya costume with long bamboo hats. Camp at Lingmithang at 4,140 m after a day-long trek of six to seven hours.

days.title: Lingmithang — Laya
days.description: The trek for the day is a downhill walk along the narrow winding river valley. The trail leads you to the west side of Laya village. At 3,850 m the campsite is on a high flat bench above the village.

days.title: Laya halt
days.description: A day halt at Laya gives us time to go around and explore the village to the fullest — its houses, its people and their unique costume and way of life.

days.title: Laya — Gasa Tsachu — Punakha
days.description: After a short descent to the army camp you meet the car and drive to Punakha. On the way we stop at the Gasa hot spring to relax the muscles and aches earned over ten days of trekking. Gasa is one of the most famous hot springs in Bhutan; in winter thousands of people come to soak here, believing in its power to heal joints, backs and many other pains and ailments. After spending enough time there, drive on to Punakha for the night.

days.title: Punakha — Thimphu — Paro
days.description: Drive to Paro via Thimphu. As the capital city, Thimphu is quite crowded — but there are no traffic lights. We visit the National Memorial Chorten, Buddha Point and the weekend market, have lunch, and drive to Paro for overnight.

days.title: Departure
days.description: After breakfast, we see you off at the airport.

title: Snowman Trek (Full)
subtitle: The full Paro-to-Bumthang traverse — one of the hardest treks on earth
overview: The Snowman Trek is the ultimate Himalayan traverse. This full Paro-to-Bumthang route links the Jomolhari base camp, Lingshi, Laya and the almost mythical district of Lunana, crossing a chain of passes — several above 5,000 m — before descending to the cultural valley of Bumthang.

It demands excellent fitness, real acclimatisation and a tolerance for remote, unpredictable weather; there are no roads, lodges or easy exits once you are in Lunana. In return it offers a wilderness experience almost unmatched anywhere on earth, from the Gophu La at 5,470 m to the hot springs of Duer Tsachu, where Guru Padmasambhava is said to have bathed.
highlights: Cross the Gophu La at 5,470 m, the highest pass of the trek
Trek through Laya and the remote district of Lunana
Views of Gangkhar Puensum, the highest unclimbed peak in the world
Bathe at the Duer Tsachu hot springs near the finish

days.title: Shana — Thangthangkha
days.description: After breakfast, the winding trail with frequent climbs and descents, crossing countless streams, leads us to our campsite in a meadow at 3,597 m — an elevation gain of 777 m.

days.title: Thangthangkha — Jangothang
days.description: Continue the trail along the Pa Chhu; the valley opens again after crossing a small army outpost. Trekking through the open valley affords views of high ridges and snow-capped mountains, with yaks and yak-herder camps on the valley floor. The day brings us near the ruined fortress at the base of Mt. Jomolhari. Camp at 4,100 m.

days.title: Jangothang halt
days.description: Hike to Tshophu, about two hours' walk from Jangothang, then come back to camp and rest to prepare for the next day.

days.title: Jangothang — Lingshi
days.description: Climb gradually toward the Nyile La (4,880 m) through wide pastureland. On your way, depending on the season, you will find yak herders in their camps. Descending from the pass to Lingshi you have a beautiful view of Lingshi Dzong, the valley, Tserim Kang and its glaciers. Camp at 4,010 m.

days.title: Lingshi — Chebisa
days.description: Today is the shortest of all days on our trip. Upon reaching Chebisa at 3,870 m, having trekked three to four hours, we camp alongside the village settlement. You can visit the village houses and experience Bhutanese rural life.

days.title: Chebisa — Shomuthang
days.description: Trekking through wide pastureland leads up to the Gobu La at approximately 4,400 m. Along the way you find some yak herders. Conquering the pass, we descend to the valley. The campsite is above a river bank, a tributary of the Mo Chhu, at 4,210 m.

days.title: Shomuthang — Robluthang
days.description: We start early, for the trek is a little strenuous. Upon crossing the Jhari La at 4,600 m we descend to the Tsharijathang valley, where you can see herds of takin, the national animal of Bhutan. Camp at 4,390 m.

days.title: Robluthang — Lingmithang
days.description: Crossing the Shinge La at 4,900 m, you take a downhill trek following the valley. Lingmithang, a beautiful village under Laya, offers an opportunity to see people dressed in typical Laya costume with long bamboo hats. Camp at 4,120 m.

days.title: Lingmithang — Laya
days.description: The trek for the day is a downhill walk along the narrow winding river valley. The trail leads you to the west side of Laya village; the campsite is on a high flat bench above the village, or in the village itself, at 3,890 m.

days.title: Laya halt
days.description: Let's rest and go around the villages, exploring the houses and the people. The Layap are ever welcoming and will readily pose for photographs. Their dress is very typical, particularly that of the women, with bamboo hats decorated with turquoise and silver ornaments. In the evening you get to be part of a cultural event with local girls performing dances.

days.title: Laya — Rodophu
days.description: After descending a while we reach the army camp. We continue following the river until the turn-off point to Rodophu. After lunch we pass through lush rhododendron until we reach camp at 4,220 m.

days.title: Rodophu — Narithang
days.description: The trail leads uphill most of the time through dwarf rhododendron bushes and barren areas with lots of ups and downs. We cross the Tshomo La (4,780 m) and descend to the campsite at Narithang (4,930 m), where yak herders keep their summer camp just below Gangla Karchung (6,395 m). Overnight at camp.

days.title: Narithang — Tarina
days.description: We start early, for today is a long stretch. We climb to the Karchung La at 5,150 m and conquer the summit, from where one can have a splendid view of Tari Gang (7,300 m). Karchung La is the point where two main rivers divide — the front of the pass is the source of the Mo Chhu at Punakha, the back the source of the Pho Chhu. After the pass we descend very deeply and steeply to the river bed; great care is needed. Camp at 4,040 m.

days.title: Tarina — Woche
days.description: We trek downhill through coniferous forest, following the upper ridges of the Pho Chhu. The trail then climbs over a ridge and drops to Woche at 3,800 m. After six to seven hours of walking, camp here for the night.

days.title: Woche — Lhedi
days.description: The trek starts through juniper and fir forest, gradually entering rhododendron. Climb to the Keche La at 4,480 m for a great view of the surrounding mountains. After the pass, descend to the riverside, walking through the village and enjoying the scenic view of mountains roofing the valley. Follow the river to Lhedi village, where one of the main sources of the Pho Chhu begins. Camp at 3,650 m.

days.title: Lhedi — Thanza
days.description: The trek continues along the bank of the river, ascending gradually to Choejung village. Cross the bridge and, after seven to eight hours of trekking, reach Thanza at 4,000 m, where we camp.

days.title: Thanza halt
days.description: We take a rest day, exploring nearby lakes and mountains. It provides a refreshing break to rejuvenate you for the rest of the trek.

days.title: Thanza — Tshorim
days.description: Having chosen the route to Bumthang, the trek starts by climbing a ridge with a great view of Table Mountain and the Thanza valley below. The ridge is at 4,500 m and rises gradually to 4,650 m. After lunch, walk upwards towards the left side of the bridge to enjoy the view of snow-capped mountains. You reach the campsite of Tshorim at 5,120 m after climbing more ridges.

days.title: Tshorim — Gophu La — Zanam
days.description: This is one of the highlights of the trek. The day starts with a short climb to Tshorim Tsho; you walk along the side of the lake enjoying a panoramic view of the Gophu La ranges. The last climb to the Gophu La (5,470 m) — the highest pass on the Paro-to-Bumthang Snowman — is very short. After the pass, descend to Zanam, walking along the ridge to enjoy a great view of Gangkhar Puensum. If interested, one can divert to the left to climb Pyramid Peak for a better view. Camp at 4,950 m.

days.title: Zanam — Menchugang
days.description: The trail follows the Sha Chhu and descends gradually to Menchugang. It is about a five- to six-hour walk, almost gently downhill all the way to camp at 4,300 m.

days.title: Menchugang — Warathang
days.description: After half an hour of gentle climbing to the Phodrang La (4,740 m), where the trail is almost invisible, the stiff climb to the Saka La (4,970 m) begins. Visibility along the Saka La trail is poor, so one must watch the top of the ridge for guidance. After lunch near a yak-herder camp you climb the pass, and the path then descends past a couple of lakes before a short, stunning ascent over the Warthang La (4,780 m). The scenery is beautiful, with small lakes and mountain peaks. Camp at 4,530 m.

days.title: Warathang — Duer Tsachu
days.description: An hour's climb leads to the Nephu La (4,600 m). After the pass you descend to the riverside through dense rhododendron, juniper and conifer forest. After the bridge a short climb leads to Duer Tsachu. These hot springs, where Guru Padmasambhava is supposed to have bathed, might be the most stunningly beautiful in the Himalaya — you may want to spend an extra day here. Camp at 3,340 m.

days.title: Duer Tsachu — Tshochenchen
days.description: From the hot springs it is a long and steady climb again, over the Gortong La (4,430 m) and Juli La (4,710 m), with great views of the mountains of Lunana. You will also come across blue lakes and yak-herder huts. The climb and the overall trek take about eight to nine hours. Camp at 3,850 m.

days.title: Tshochenchen — Duer village (trek ends)
days.description: This is the last day of the trek. The path follows the Chamkhar Chhu, descending gradually with a few climbs in between. The trek ends when you arrive at Duer village, from where you drive to Jakar in Bumthang.

days.title: Bumthang — Paro
days.description: After an early breakfast, start your journey to the west again. Overnight in Paro.

days.title: Departure
days.description: After breakfast, we see you off at the airport.

title: Snowman Trek II — Paro to Nikachhu
subtitle: The full western approach, then south through Lunana to the Nikachhu
overview: Snowman II walks the whole classic approach from Paro: the Pa Chhu to the Jomolhari base camp at Jangothang, over the Nyile La to Lingshi, through Chebisa and the takin valley of Tsharijathang to Laya.

From Laya it climbs into Lunana over the Tshomo La and Karchung La, through Woche, Lhedi and Thanza, then turns south over the Jazi La to Tshochena, Jichu Dramo — the highest camp of the trek — Chukarpo and Tampa Tsho, finishing at Marothang above the Nikachhu. Its length, altitude, remoteness and weather make it every bit as serious as the full traverse.

Takin herds in the Tsharijathang valley, and a rest day at Laya
Camp at Jichu Dramo (5,250 m), the highest camp of the trek
A chain of remote Lunana lakes on the way south

title: Snowman Trek III — Gasa to Bumthang
subtitle: Lunana and the Gangkhar Puensum base camp, finishing in Bumthang
overview: Snowman III keeps the great eastern half of the traverse — Lunana, the Gophu La and the descent to Bumthang — while replacing the long Paro approach with a drive up through Thimphu and Punakha to Taktse Makhang below Laya.

From Laya the route runs over the Tshomo La and Karchung La into Lunana, through Woche, Lhedi and Thanza, and on to Tshorim and the base camp of Gangkhar Puensum, the highest unclimbed mountain in the world. It finishes with the long descent to the Duer Tsachu hot springs — where Guru Padmasambhava is said to have bathed — and out along the Chamkhar Chhu to Bumthang.
highlights: Camp at the Gangkhar Puensum base camp (4,970 m)
Cross the Gophu La (5,230 m) and Karchung La (5,150 m)
Bathe at the Duer Tsachu hot springs
Finish in Bumthang, the cultural heartland of Bhutan

title: Snowman Trek IV — Laya to Nikachhu
subtitle: The shortest way into Lunana, starting from Laya
overview: Snowman IV drives in via Thimphu and Punakha to Taktse Makhang below Laya, saving the six trekking days that the full route spends walking up from Paro. From Laya it follows the classic Snowman line over the Tshomo La and Karchung La into Lunana, through Woche, Lhedi and Thanza.

From Thanza the trail turns south over the Jazi La to a string of remote lakes — Tshochena, Jichu Dramo, Tampa Tsho — and finishes at Marothang above the Nikachhu, from where a six- to seven-hour drive returns you to Paro. Everything about it is remote: no roads, no lodges and no easy exits once you are in Lunana.
highlights: Reach Laya by road, saving six days of approach trekking
Camp at Jichu Dramo (5,250 m), the highest camp of the trek
Cross the Karchung La (5,150 m) and the Jazi La (5,090 m)
Lakes and glacier landscapes all the way down to Marothang

After crossing the pass we descend very steeply to the river bed; care is needed on the descent.

days.title: Tarina — Woche
days.description: We trek downhill through coniferous forest, following the upper ridges of the Pho Chhu. The trail then climbs over a ridge and drops to Woche at 3,800 m. After six to seven hours of walking, camp here for the night.

days.title: Woche — Lhedi
days.description: The trek starts through juniper and fir forest, gradually entering rhododendron. Climb to the Keche La at 4,480 m, where one has a great view of the surrounding mountains. After the pass, descend to the riverside, walking through the village and enjoying the scenic view of mountains roofing the valley. Follow the river to Lhedi village, where one of the main sources of the Pho Chhu begins. Camp at 3,650 m.

days.title: Lhedi — Thanza
days.description: The trek continues along the bank of the river, ascending gradually to Choejung village. Cross the bridge and, after seven to eight hours of trekking, reach Thanza at 4,000 m, where we camp.

days.title: Thanza halt
days.description: We take a rest day, exploring nearby lakes and mountains. It provides a refreshing break to rejuvenate you for the rest of the trek.

days.title: Thanza — Tshochena
days.description: Climb for almost five hours to cross the Jazi La at about 5,090 m. After crossing the pass, descend for almost two hours to the campsite.

days.title: Tshochena — Jichu Dramo
days.description: Jichu Dramo is almost seven hours' walk from Tshochena. There is no pass on the way and you see many beautiful lakes. Along the way you can also see beautiful flowers such as Meconopsis superba and many other medicinal plants. Camp at 5,250 m — the highest campsite on the trek.

days.title: Jichu Dramo — Chukarpo
days.description: It takes approximately seven hours to reach the campsite. You climb for almost four hours to reach the Gangrinche Zoe pass, then descend for three to four hours to camp.

days.title: Chukarpo — Tampa Tsho
days.description: Tampa Tsho is six hours from Chukarpo. Walk along the riverside for approximately three and a half hours, then climb for almost two and a half hours to the campsite. Near the camp you see a very beautiful lake and landscape.

days.title: Tampa Tsho — Marothang (trek ends)
days.description: It takes almost seven hours to reach Marothang. Climb for two hours to reach the pass at 4,800 m, then descend for five hours, finding lakes and beautiful glacier landscapes on the way. Overnight at camp — our last night in tents.

days.title: Marothang — Paro
days.description: From Marothang we drive to Paro. The drive takes about six to seven hours. Overnight in Paro.

days.title: Departure
days.description: Our team will take you to the airport for your departure.
